title: Harry Carney and Sonny Greer
summary: Carney joined 1927, Hodges 1928, Cootie 1929; Cootie says Sonny Greer fit the band as no one else could, and liked Louis Bellson.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. So really, everybody was very happy in those days.
Well, when Harry came in -- did you come in ahead of Harry?
He came in ahead of you.
Harry came in 1927 and Johnny came in 1928, and I came in 1929.

Is that right? Well, cause I always think of -- always thought of Harry as, you know, he was so modest and young looking and acting and everything. I mean, he didn't throw his weight around at all, did he?
No. No, no. No, he didn't have no weight during that time.
He had Barney and Johnny at that time.
No, he didn't have no weight.
Well, Duke built those parts and every-
-thing. Duke brought Harry right out, didn't he?
I mean, he built it right in there for him, didn't he?
For Harry to fall right into that picture.

He and Barney was from New Orleans, and they had that New Orleans thing going, you know. So that's the reason why they would be over there talking that half Creole stuff, and we didn't like that so much.
That's funny, isn't it? Well, where did Sonny fit in there? Well, he's just --
He's always acted blow top, didn't he?
Yeah. He -- yeah, Sonny. I don't know where was Sonny. He'd be thinking about getting that next
And, I mean, being Duke's equal. Being Duke's co-whatever, you know?
Because the fact that he was somebody before Duke got to New York, that was something that Sonny didn't let anybody forget. Right.
But Sonny could play drums, though, couldn't he? If he kept his mind on the business. Or would you say so, Cootie?
Yeah. During that era. During that era of time, he could.
Before those arrangements -- before the band got bigger, and the arrangements got more complicated.
He fit the band. I didn't think nobody could come in that band and fit it but Sonny.
But I liked Louis Bellson when he came with the band.
I liked the sound with the band.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, he -- I mean, he had everything, the facility and everything, to go with the concept and everything, didn't he?
I think Sam Woodyard really provided a sound in that band that really sounded right, didn't he?
How long was Sam with that band?
Ten years, wasn't he? Or some --
You know I wasn't there then.
